correctness.rationale: The digit-sum identity modulo B-1 gives (p-1)(q-1)=1 modulo B-1. Modulo 2 this leaves only 4 in odd bases, which is checked exactly. For even bases, compatible distinct-prime residues are parametrized by the involution T(r)=1+(r-1)^(-1); CRT gives the exact residue count. Fixed-modulus PNT in arithmetic progressions plus Mertens estimates and Brun--Titchmarsh yield the stated prime-pair main term, while prime squares are lower order.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact all-odd-base classification and an explicit analytic sieve for every even base, turning a known digit-sum congruence into a base-parity structural law and a prime-pair density constant. It is an infinite-family statement across all bases and is not a bounded recomputation of the decimal sequence.
